title: HA/DR automation: multi-AZ private installer + Helm/Terraform runbooks-as-code
author: Priya Singh
release_notes: Adds automated HA/DR runbooks-as-code and infra modules for private deployments. Includes Terraform multi-AZ networking module, Helm chart changes for anti-affinity and topology-aware PV scheduling, installer orchestration hooks for failover and restore drills, and a set of automated restore-playbooks. Backwards compatible; opt-in via feature flags.
description: Motivation: customers running Redwood Private requested automated, tested HA/DR tooling for multi-AZ private installs and on-prem deployments. This PR implements a runbooks-as-code approach so runbooks can be executed and audited, adds Terraform modules to provision multi-AZ network topology and DR-ready subnets, and updates Helm charts and the private-installer to support automated failover and restore drills. Changes: 1) terraform/modules/network-multi-az: new module to create AZ-aware subnets, NAT/IGW, route53 health checks and failover records; 2) private-installer: orchestration hooks to run pre-upgrade snapshot, post-upgrade KV reconciliation, and automated failover tests; 3) helm/redwood: podAntiAffinity defaults, topology-aware persistentVolumeClaims and crash-loop backoff improvements for faster restarts; 4) runbooks/as-code: playbooks (ansible) and a runner that can execute and report runbook steps to the console and to the audit log; 5) ci/workflows: add e2e-restore-drill job and terraform plan check. Testing and validation: added unit tests for the installer hooks, end-to-end restore drill smoke test (runs in CI against a staged k8s cluster), terraform fmt/validate in CI, and manual multi-AZ restore drill performed in staging (logs linked). Rollback and safety: all automation gated behind a new feature flag ENABLE_HA_DR_AUTOMATION=false by default; installer changes include explicit dry-run and approval step for dangerous operations. Docs: added runbooks and a runbook index page with expected SLAs, run durations, and escalation steps. See runbooks link for operational playbooks. Checklist: migration steps and data back-compat considered; no breaking changes to existing private installs unless feature flag enabled. This description is a single continuous string as required.

operational_impact: Low by default; feature gated. When enabled, runbooks may trigger snapshot and restore operations which will be clearly logged and require explicit approval for destructive steps.
migration_notes: Existing clusters are unaffected until ENABLE_HA_DR_AUTOMATION is turned on. Storage class topology may require admin review; documentation lists steps to add required annotations and to test in staging.
notes_for_release: Opt-in HA/DR automation for Private; add to release notes under 'Private Deployments' with instructions to enable the feature flag and link to runbooks.
security_considerations: Runner authenticates with a service principal scoped to runbook operations. All sensitive operations require KMS-encrypted snapshots and audit logging. Reviewed by security.
backout_plan: Dry-run mode available; installer supports rollback to previous version and restore from pre-upgrade snapshot. Runbooks include automated rollback steps and manual escalation contacts.
